identity_baseline.why: the baseline IS cell A, so every Δ is computed against itself

same_style_150.note: original-style similarity change + content preservation only; no margin is reported or mixed into the 600 table

historical_750.scope: all 750 pairs, historical compatibility only (P0 threshold 0.50523 refers to this)

definitions.S_t: target-style similarity; S_c = same score vs the SOURCE style
definitions.csd_score: cosine(CSD 768-d style descriptor, L2-normalised prototype); prototype = mean of the first 74 frozen train-pool descriptors
definitions.dino_score: max cosine over the style's 30 test references (the official dino_style_similarity)
definitions.dino_S_c_caveat: with ref_pool='first' the 30 references of a style ARE the 30 test sources of that style, so S_c(baseline) = 1.0 by self-match and any transformation pushes DINO ΔS negative.  CSD (train-pool prototype, no self-match) is therefore the primary line.
definitions.patch_swd: sliced Wasserstein (L1, 32 random directions, 256-point quantile grid) between DINOv2 patch-token distributions of the image and the frozen target-style train pool; reported as swd_base - swd_gen
definitions.quadrant: sign of (ΔT, ΔS); T+/S- = toward target and away from source

protocol.pairs: 600 cross-style response pairs (150 sources x 4 non-self targets)
protocol.excluded: 150 same-style pairs are reported separately, never mixed in here
protocol.tolerance_note: no success threshold is applied; all numbers are descriptive

provenance_csd.backbone: CLIP ViT-L/14 visual encoder (224px, patch 14, width 1024, 24 layers, 16 heads)
provenance_csd.preprocess: Resize(shorter side 224, bicubic) -> CenterCrop(224) -> ToTensor -> CLIP mean/std
provenance_csd.feature_extraction: backbone CLS (1024-d) projected by last_layer_style -> L2 normalised (768-d)
provenance_csd.similarity: cosine (= inner product of L2-normalised descriptors)
provenance_csd.upstream_caveat: official README (2024-10-03) flags a known discrepancy of the uploaded weights vs the numbers reported in the paper
